        - What exists: a `RETURNED_PAYMENT` correction C (a bounced Payment) recovers every Refund paid from the Payment's value that is not fully returned (a `RECOVERED_BY_CHARGE` of its whole net, a charge to the person who received it), reverses every Credit application and Deposit application from the Payment's Credits and Deposits, then reverses the Credits (taking all they still hold) and the Deposit receipts (each funded Deposit ends empty). A `DEPOSIT_RECEIPT_CORRECTION` C does the same for one Deposit's wrong receipt (recoveries, applications reversed newest first, the whole receipt reversed, the Deposit empty), and may then write the right receipt with its own DL-032 step (10e-2b) or forfeiture (10e-2c), all from the new money. The walk counts C's draw as what it paid out (the Credit or receipt reversal, plus any new applications, Refunds and forfeitures) less what it brought back (its recoveries, its application reversals and new receipts), so C takes from a return E exactly E's money still in the source at C's time; the placed function does not split such a C and names its reversal as one open part (`CREDIT_REVERSAL`, `RECEIPT_REVERSAL`). A part of E's money on another correction S's payment that C reversed stops open in the follow function (a reversal by another correction kind: `CHANGED_APPLICATION`), and a part on S's Refund that C recovered is above that Refund's net (`CHANGED_REFUND`). E's reversal is refused today in all three cases (the committed real-path tests `test_settlement_returned_value_left_migration.py::test_a_payment_return_and_a_receipt_correction_count_what_they_take_from_a_return`, the owner's two examples, and `test_settlement_return_reversal_changed_payment_migration.py::test_a_part_on_a_payment_a_receipt_correction_reversed_waits`).
        - Rule: in all three shapes the money went back into the source (C's recovery or application reversal) and out with C's reversal of the source, and C charged E's returned Refund R's recipient only R's net, which E had lowered. So E's reversal charges each such part back to the person who received R (a further `RECOVERED_BY_CHARGE` on R linked to the reversal, the 10e-1c charge to that person on R's charge Lease or with no Lease, the Q-2026-10-12-94 recipient rule), and nothing else: the charges C made to other Refunds' recipients and the debts C made owed again stay. - **Signature fixture clock (owner instruction of 2026-10-14; test set-up only; record ops/reviews/V1-056-signature-fixture-clock.md)**: the `Signature evidence is invalid` failures of the Lease signature fixture (a full rerun in four sessions; 13 failures at the end of 10e-3e run P3) come from `app.record_lease_signature`, which refuses a signing time later than the database's statement time with no tolerance (migration 24; `app.sign_lease` the same), while the fixtures took the time from the host clock (`datetime.now(UTC)`) and the database runs in the Docker VM, whose clock can lag the host clock; a lag longer than the few milliseconds between the fixture's reading and the database statement is enough, far below the about 80 ms resolution of the K1 check; the failures cluster in one stretch of a run (drift, then a resync). Fix in the test set-up only: `database_now()` in `test_lease_lifecycle_migration.py` reads `clock_timestamp()` from the database; `signature_command`'s default and every `LeaseSignCommand` and HTTP signing time in the database tests use it, and the lifecycle test's termination time too (it must not be before the signing time); the app's check is not changed.
- **Signing time from the database clock (owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-14-110, 2026-10-14; small sub-slice, built first in the order of 2026-10-14; BR-AUDIT-003, API-036, API-038, UI-038, UI-040; no migration; record ops/reviews/V1-056-signing-time-database-clock.md)**: a Signer's signature time and the Lease signing time are the database's own time at the moment of the command, never a browser or device clock, so a device clock ahead of the database can no longer refuse a signing and nobody can make a signature look earlier by setting a device clock back.
  - Pre-code design (2026-10-14, read only, head `20261208_134`): (1) Routes (`backend/src/property_rental/lease_api.py`): `LeaseSignatureSource` (`PATCH /lease-signers/{signer_id}`) and `LeaseSignSource` (`POST /leases/{lease_id}/sign`) drop `signed_at`; both keep `extra="forbid"`, so a body that still sends a signing time is refused (422) and nothing is called; both routes pass `signed_at=None` to the service. (2) Service (`backend/src/property_rental/lease.py`): `LeaseRecordSignatureCommand.signed_at` and `LeaseSignCommand.signed_at` become `datetime | None` (a given time must still carry a time zone); the two calls pass `COALESCE(%s::timestamptz, statement_timestamp())`, so with `None` the database function receives the statement time that its own check compares with (`statement_timestamp()` is the same inside the called function). No database function changes: the checks stay as they are (a time later than the statement time, a time before the Signer was added, a Lease signing before a Signer's signature are still refused). The request digest carries `signed_at: null`, and the database replays a known request before it reads the time, so a retry of the same request returns the first result with its first time. Implementer's reading (named in the report): the service command keeps the optional explicit time so the committed database tests keep checking the refusals they check today through the service with explicit times (a Signer signature time later than the statement time; a Lease signing time earlier than a Signer's signature or later than the statement time; the "not before the Signer was added" check is unchanged but has no committed test, corrected in review round 2); no route passes one. (3) Screen and client (`frontend/src/leaseClient.ts`, `frontend/src/LeaseManagement.tsx`): `LeaseSignatureSource` drops `signed_at`; the screen no longer sends `new Date().toISOString()`; it shows the time the server returns, as before. (6) Docs: docs/002 BR-AUDIT-003, docs/005 API-036 and API-038, docs/006 UI-040, docs/010; traceability appended. So money the Credit holds for other reasons stays refundable through the ordinary draft (owner's option (b): "money a Customer's Credit holds for other reasons stays refundable"), and the returned money leaves only through a correction. Implementer's reading for the reviewers: the refusal compares the amount with the money other than the returned money (available less left), not the whole Credit, because both are in one Credit and money in a Credit has no identity; a left value above what the Credit holds (the known limit: ordinary Credit applications are not counted) refuses every ordinary Refund of that Credit (fail closed). Money example: the Settlement refunded 300.00 of Credit C; correction X1 records that the 300.00 came back, so C holds 300.00 and X1 has 300.00 left; an `EXTRA_CHARGE` correction bills 100.00. ## 4. Questions for the owner (with my recommendation)

Blocking questions are marked (B). I will not start a slice whose question is open.

1. (B, slice 1) Making the Lease draft and sign functions reject a non-month-end End Date is a tightening change. Does DL-069 ("V1-056 adds the validation") count as owner approval for this one tightening? Recommendation: yes, function check only, no table CHECK, existing rows untouched, historical fixtures narrowed with docs/010 notes.
2. (slice 1) The End Date is optional on a Lease draft. Recommendation: check it only when present, and require a month-end End Date at signing.
3. (B, slice 2) Which existing capability lets Staff record each draft kind? Recommendation: Refund drafts `refunds.create`; forfeiture and Deposit use `deposits.dispose`; Payment move the existing allocation reversal capability; Final Settlement and corrections need a preparer capability that does not exist. Options: reuse `deposits.dispose`, or approve a new `final_settlements.prepare`. I recommend the new `final_settlements.prepare` because SEC-020 lists "prepare and close Final Settlements" as its own family; this needs your answer.
4. (B, slice 2) May the same person prepare and confirm a draft (for example the Owner alone)? Recommendation: allowed, both actors recorded, because SEC-022 says the system must not require two people; you can still give Staff only the prepare capability.
5. (slice 2) Draft life: Recommendation: a draft can be rejected (approver) or withdrawn (preparer) with a reason; no expiry; confirm fails if the underlying balances changed since the draft.
6. (B, slices 3 and 6) Existing direct paths run at once today: Credit Refunds, Pet Refunds, Reservation Deposit Refunds and dispositions, and termination deposit dispositions. BR-AUTH-010 says Refunds and deposit forfeiture are drafts. Recommendation: from V1-056 every new Refund and every Deposit forfeiture (Lease and Reservation) goes through a draft; the old direct routes return a clear error pointing to the draft route; old records stay unchanged. This changes existing API behavior and existing tests. Please confirm, or limit drafts to Lease-related actions only.
7. (slice 3) Refund methods: one global list like Payment Methods, or per Property? Recommendation: global, like `app.payment_methods`.
8. (slice 5) Does the hand-back VOID or credit Adjustment need a draft and `financial.approve`? BR-AUTH-010 does not list it. Recommendation: no draft; existing `invoices.void` and `invoices.adjust` with a reason.
9. (slice 5) Partly paid hand-back Invoice: the credit Adjustment removes the unpaid rest of every line (Rent and fixed Service lines), consistent with the whole-Invoice VOID. Recommendation: yes, per line.
10. (B, slice 6) How does the system know the forfeiture ground? Termination bases today are `VOLUNTARY_EARLY`, `CUSTOMER_VIOLATION`, `SIGNED_LEASE_OTHER` and `UNPAID_INITIAL_OBLIGATION`; pet versus non-pet violation and the 30-day Rent nonpayment default are not separate bases. Recommendation: the forfeiture draft takes the ground from the termination record (governing rule and linked warnings or Serious Default event) and refuses when it cannot be derived; no new termination basis.
11. (slice 6) Existing disposition functions may accept a partial forfeiture amount. Requiring the full amount for new forfeitures rejects input that was accepted before. Recommendation: enforce full amount only in the new draft path; leave the old function as is (it is no longer reachable once Q6 is approved).
12. (slice 6) "Valid pet damage" means move-out inspection findings with `pet_related = true` that were billed as Damage charges. Recommendation: yes; nothing else counts unless staff link it with a reason.
13. (B, slice 4) Is the cleaning charge issued by an explicit staff command, or created by the system at move-out? Rules say nothing is automatic. Recommendation: explicit command; Final Settlement preview shows a blocking issue until it is issued (or the Customer never moved in).
14. (slice 4) Which Invoice carries it, and what if the Unit has no rate? Recommendation: its own one-time charge Invoice at move-out (the final Utility Invoice may be issued at a different time); a Unit with no configured rate blocks the charge until a rate is set. A rate of 0 is allowed and gives no charge line.
15. (B, slice 10) Post-settlement correction kinds. BR-SETTLE-013 names "extra charge or Refund". Recommendation: only those two kinds in V1-056 (a linked one-time charge Invoice, or a linked Refund draft). Reversal of a Settlement Deposit application or of a Credit application waits for a later owner decision.
16. (slice 7) Payment move limits. Recommendation: same Property only; the whole wrong allocation moves; if the target Invoice owes less, the rest stays as unallocated Payment value (not Credit) until the normal recognition rules apply.
17. Security reviews for slices 5 and 10 in addition to the required ones? Recommendation: yes.
18. Existing tests that assert immediate Refund or disposition behavior will need narrowing if Q6 is approved. Recommendation: narrow only the one expectation per test, keep test names, docs/010 note per test, as the run rules require.

### 7.1 What exists today (read-only survey, 2026-10-21)

Accounts and password storage
- `app.user_accounts` (migration `20260817_02`): `actor_id`, `normalized_username` (unique), `display_name`, `audit_name`, `lifecycle_state` (`active`, `disabled`), `mfa_policy_class` (`required`, `optional`), provenance. There is **no account class column** (`owner`, `manager`, `staff`). `administrative_recovery.py` and `account_recovery.py` take the account class as "provider-established" input; nothing stores it.
- `app.password_credentials` (migration `20260817_03`, not opened): read by `PostgresLocalAccountRepository.find_by_username` in `local_authentication.py` (`verifier_encoding`).
- `password_security.py`: `PasswordHashService` (Argon2id, `RFC_9106_LOW_MEMORY`, NFC before hashing and verifying). It has **no length or blocklist rule**. The 15 to 128 code point rule (`PASSWORD_MIN_CODE_POINTS`, `PASSWORD_MAX_CODE_POINTS`) and the blocklist check live only in `initial_owner_bootstrap.py` (`BootstrapPasswordPolicy`). The admin recovery request model checks only `min_length=15, max_length=128` in pydantic (`AdministrativeRecoveryRequest` in `access_admin_api.py`), with no NFC or blocklist step.
- `app.actor_identities` (kind `HUMAN` or `SERVICE`) and `app.assert_active_financial_actor` check that a human actor is an active `user_accounts` row. The database never checks a capability; every financial function trusts the capability the service checked.

Sign-in, sessions and CSRF
- `local_authentication.py`: `LocalAuthenticationService.authenticate` (dummy verifier for unknown names, one generic rejection) and `BoundedAuthenticationAttemptLimiter` (in memory, per process, rolling window, configurable limits per account and per source). The limiter **counts every attempt, also correct ones**, before the password is checked; it forgets everything on restart and is not shared between worker processes. No 5-tries or 15-minute values are set anywhere.
- `browser_session.py`: `BrowserSessionLifetimeService` with `INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT` 30 minutes and `ABSOLUTE_LIFETIME` 24 hours. `app.browser_sessions` (migration `20260819_07`): sha256 token verifier, `last_activity_at`, `idle_expires_at`, `absolute_expires_at` (`CHECK = created_at + 24 hours`), revocation columns, lifecycle trigger, history-destruction guard. `session_revocation.py`: `SessionRevocationService` with `APPROVED_REVOCATION_TRIGGERS`.
- `auth_api.py` (`create_auth_router`, prefix `/api/v1/auth`): `POST /login`, `POST /mfa/challenge`, `POST /mfa/enrollment`, `POST /mfa/enrollment/confirm`, `GET /session`, `POST /logout`, `POST /reauthenticate`, `POST /recovery-codes`, `POST /recovery-codes/regenerate`. Cookies `__Host-prm_session`, `__Host-prm_preauth`, `__Host-prm_csrf` (Secure, HttpOnly except CSRF). The router talks to an `AuthenticationFlow` protocol; the only implementation is `UnavailableAuthenticationFlow`, so every sign-in answers "unavailable".
- `browser_security.py`: `require_browser_mutation` (exact `Origin` equal to `Settings.allowed_browser_origin`, which must be `https://...`, plus double-submit `X-CSRF-Token`). Used by most mutation routes, directly or through helpers such as `_mutation` in `allocation_receipt_api.py`.

MFA and recovery
- `totp_security.py` (`TotpService`, `Aes256GcmTotpSecretProtector` with a key identifier), `mfa_policy.py` (`MfaActorEstablishmentService`: no normal actor before required MFA), TOTP enrollments table (migration `20260819_06`).
- Recovery codes: `recovery_code_security.py`, `recovery_code_issuance.py`, `recovery_code_consumption.py`, `recovery_code_lifecycle.py`, `recovery_code_regeneration.py`, verifier table (migration `20260817_04`).
- Account recovery: `account_recovery.py` (`AccountRecoveryService`, `TrustedAccountRecoveryAuthorizer`, `PostgresAccountRecoveryRepository`), `app.perform_account_recovery` and the append-only `app.account_recovery_audit_events` (migration `20260819_08`; modes `recovery_code`, `administrative`, `emergency`; it can set a new verifier, reset MFA, consume a recovery code and revoke sessions in one call).
- Owner reset of Manager and Staff (DL-058, API-099): `AdministrativeRecoveryAuthorizationService` in `administrative_recovery.py` allows only `owner_to_manager` and `owner_to_staff`; route `POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/administrative-recovery` in `access_admin_api.py`. **Today the Owner types the new password**, with an optional `reset_mfa`; there is no one-time password, no 24-hour limit and no forced change.

First Owner
- `initial_owner_bootstrap.py` and `bootstrap_cli.py` (DL-059): password only from `/dev/tty`; database URL from descriptor 3, TOTP protection key from descriptor 4 (must be a root-owned regular file with mode 0600, 32 bytes or 64 hex characters), blocklist from descriptor 5; 10 recovery codes shown once on the TTY; `prm_bootstrap` identity only; closure tables in migrations `20260818_05` and `20260820_09`.

Capabilities, bundles, administration
- `identity.py`: `AuthenticatedActor` (actor id plus `CapabilityGrant`s with Property and object scopes), `is_authorized` (exact grant), `deny_unauthenticated_actor`.
- `app.py`: `create_app(actor_resolver=deny_unauthenticated_actor, authentication_flow=None, access_administration_flow=None, ...)`; the module-level `app = create_app()` therefore denies every protected route with 401, and every sign-in is unavailable.
- `access_admin_api.py` (`identity.manage_access`): user list, create, update, revoke sessions, capability list, role bundle list, create, update, assignment, authorization history, administrative recovery. Only `UnavailableAccessAdministrationFlow` exists. Its checks also need object-scoped grants (`user_account`, `role_bundle`).
- **No capability catalog table, no role bundle table, no assignment table, no default bundle seed** (DL-074 facts confirmed). Capabilities are code constants, about 70 today (for example `financial.approve`, `final_settlements.prepare`, `payments.record`, `payments.allocate`, `leases.sign`, `reservations.extend`, `leases.terminate`, `invoices.void`, `service_rates.manage`, `utility_rates.manage`, `property.manage`, `configuration.read`, `exchange_rates.manage`, `audit.view`, `identity.read_self`, `identity.manage_access`); `billing.generate` belongs to the billing service principal only. (Corrected by the L1b-1 review and Q-2026-10-21-161 (a): people also start billing runs and read their status with `billing.generate`; it is a bundle capability.)
- Settings checks today (`configuration_api.py`, `property_api.py`, `invoice.py`, `unit_api.py`): `configuration.read`; `service_rates.manage`; `utility_rates.manage`; `exchange_rates.manage`; `property.manage` (Property update and configuration, the one-time charge due-days setting, Unit create and update, the Unit cleaning rate under migration `20261016_81`, and some reads in `refund.py` and `unpaid_initial_termination.py`).
- Health: `GET /api/v1/health/live` and `GET /api/v1/health/ready` (`api.py`) are unauthenticated by design. `GET /api/v1/operations/status` is not built.

Routes open or under-guarded today (176 routes surveyed)
- Unauthenticated by design: the two health routes and the nine `/api/v1/auth` routes.
- Signed-in only, with no capability and no Property scope check: `GET /properties/{property_id}` (`property_api.py`), `GET /properties/{property_id}/units`, `GET /units/{unit_id}` and `GET /units/{unit_id}/timeline` (`unit_api.py`).
- Mutations with no Origin or CSRF check: `POST /properties/{property_id}/units` and `PATCH /units/{unit_id}` (`unit_api.py`).
- Every other route resolves the actor and checks a capability (in the route or in its flow). Because the resolver denies everyone, none of them is reachable today.

Frontend
- `authClient.ts` (sign-in, MFA challenge, enrollment, session read, reauthentication, recovery codes, logout; `credentials: "include"`; reads the CSRF cookie and sends `X-CSRF-Token`), `adminClient.ts` (users, bundles, assignments, recovery). `App.tsx` already has a sign-in form, MFA challenge and enrollment screens, the session-expiry return to sign-in (UI-111) and logout. Every other client calls the API with the cookie and the CSRF header. The session read (`SessionData`) has the actor id but **no display name**, so the shell cannot show the signed-in person's name. All frontend tests use mocked APIs; no browser check is possible today.
- Local running: `compose.yaml` has PostgreSQL only; `make dev` starts the API on `http://127.0.0.1:8000`; `frontend/vite.config.ts` has no proxy and no HTTPS. `__Host-` Secure cookies and the `https://` Origin rule mean the browser sign-in cannot work locally until a same-origin HTTPS setup exists (Q-2026-10-21-159).

### 7.2 Design in short

- The capability catalog, the role bundles and the assignments become tables. The default Owner, Manager and Staff bundles are seeded data for the Property (DL-074 answer 1); they stay configurable through API-080.
- A new `account_class` column (`owner`, `manager`, `staff`) on `app.user_accounts` ties the Owner-only rights to the account class, not to a bundle name (DL-058, DL-074 answer 2, SEC-021).
- One actor resolver (`PostgresSessionActorResolver`) replaces `deny_unauthenticated_actor` when a database is configured. It reads the session cookie, checks the session (idle and absolute expiry, revocation, lifecycle, completed MFA where required), updates the activity time, and builds the `CapabilityGrant`s fresh from the database on every request: the union of the user's assigned bundles, plus `settings.manage` from the per-user grant, plus `settings.manage` always for the Owner account class (and, by Q-2026-10-21-162 (b), `identity.manage_access` for the Owner account class only). Because the grants are read on every request, a removed capability stops working at the next request (SEC-017 "material privilege reduction"); disabling, resetting and MFA changes also revoke the sessions.
- `PostgresAuthenticationFlow` implements the existing `AuthenticationFlow` protocol; `PostgresAccessAdministrationFlow` implements `AccessAdministrationFlow`. `create_app` wires them, and the resolver, when `APP_DATABASE_URL` is set; tests keep injecting their own.
- Failed sign-ins are counted in the database (survive restarts, shared by workers): 5 wrong tries for one username start a 15-minute wait, with one message for every case (DL-080 item 10).
- One shared password rule in `password_security.py` (`validate_new_password`: 15 to 128 code points before and after NFC, local blocklist), used by bootstrap, the one-time password change and every later password change.
- Proposed capability names (Q-2026-10-21-151, Q-2026-10-21-158, Q-2026-10-21-160): `settings.manage` (Settings access; per user only, never in a bundle), `operations.status.read` (health page), `units.read` and `property.read` (today's signed-in-only reads).

### 7.3 Sub-slices

Each sub-slice ends in one local checkpoint commit with explicit paths, the standard secret scan and a diff scan, an independent review and a security review (every sub-slice touches sign-in or authorization), the review record under `ops/reviews/V1-056-login-<sub-slice>.md`, and one line in ops/NOW.md. Migrations are additive or relaxing only; numbers continue after `20270117_174`. Every new test gets a traceability entry appended to `ops/traceability.json` (append only; the first 1,598 entries and the guard hashes are never touched). Docs are updated in the sub-slice that changes the rule they describe. Runs follow ops/V1_055_RUN_RULES.md (migration-only check first, one targeted PostgreSQL run after a read-only search of all backend tests, full unit and full PostgreSQL runs before the commit, frontend checks for L7). A sub-slice whose question is open does not start.

#### L1a — Account class (needs Q-2026-10-21-152)
- Builds: an additive migration that adds `account_class` (`owner`, `manager`, `staff`) to `app.user_accounts`, nullable for old rows, set to `owner` for the actor named by the initial Owner bootstrap closure; a check that new rows carry a class and that at most one `owner` row exists (under the Q-152 answer); a guard that the class never changes after creation (like `app.reject_user_account_actor_id_change`); the bootstrap function writes `owner`. The `mfa_policy_class` of an `owner` or `manager` row must be `required` (DL-056). `RecoveryAccount` callers read the class from the table instead of trusting input. An account with no class can never sign in (fail closed).
- Rules: DB-AUTH-001, DL-056, DL-058, DL-059, DL-074 answer 2, SEC-013, SEC-021, SEC-072, SEC-074.
- Files: new migration; `initial_owner_bootstrap.py` (writes the class, if the bootstrap function needs a new argument the old one stays and the migration adds a new definition); `administrative_recovery.py`, `account_recovery.py` (read the class); docs/004 DB-AUTH-001.
- Tests (replaced by the pre-code design below: a separate relation, not a column): migration tests (column, check, one-Owner rule, no change after creation, backfill from the closure, `owner` and `manager` rows refused with `optional` MFA, privileges unchanged for `prm_runtime`), bootstrap tests extended (TEST-133, TEST-134: the bootstrapped Owner has class `owner`, a second `owner` row is refused), recovery tests read the stored class (TEST-130).
- Risks: an existing development database may hold accounts with no known class; they stay unable to sign in until the Owner sets them (no data is changed or deleted). (Replaced by the pre-code design below: an old unclassified account is never classified; the Owner disables it and creates a new account.) Changing the bootstrap function's definition touches a protected one-time boundary: the change is limited to writing the class, and the bootstrap least-privilege tests must still pass unchanged.
- Pre-code design (2026-10-21, after the owner's approval; read-only survey of `20260817_02`, `20260818_05`, `20260819_08`, `20260820_09`, `account_recovery.py`, `administrative_recovery.py`, `local_authentication.py` and the committed tests that insert `app.user_accounts`):
  - Migration `20270118_175` (additive), as first designed: (1) `app.user_accounts` gains `account_class text` (nullable, `CHECK (account_class IN ('owner','manager','staff'))`); (2) a table check that an `owner` or `manager` row has `mfa_policy_class = 'required'`; (3) backfill of `owner` for the actor named by `app.initial_owner_bootstrap_closure`; (4) a partial unique index for at most one `owner`; (5) a trigger that refuses any change of the class; (6) `app.establish_initial_owner_bootstrap` replaced with the same signature and body except that it writes the class (one exact-text change; owner, ACL, definer flag and settings kept by `CREATE OR REPLACE`, so a closed bootstrap stays closed).
  - Design change 1 (for the reviewers, under the design-change run rule): the plan's "a check that new rows carry a class" is not built as a table check, because about 100 committed test set-ups (14 modules) insert `app.user_accounts` rows without a class as the migration owner. Fail closed instead: an account with no class cannot be found for sign-in (`PostgresLocalAccountRepository.find_by_username` joins the class), is not resolved for recovery, and gets no grants (L1b); no application role may insert accounts or classes, and every account-creating function (the bootstrap now, the L2 create) writes a class.
  - Design change 2 (found by targeted run T1, cause B; for the reviewers, under the design-change run rule): the class is a separate append-only relation `app.user_account_classes` instead of a column, because `ALTER TABLE app.user_accounts ADD COLUMN` (and `ADD CONSTRAINT ... CHECK`) needs an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and the committed `test_migrations.py::test_v1_042_upgrade_front_door_gate_prevents_service_writer_deadlock` (a whole-chain upgrade that holds the V1-042 validation gate while a writer that already reads `app.user_accounts` waits at the gate) then deadlocks. `CREATE TABLE ... REFERENCES` and `CREATE TRIGGER` take only SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on `app.user_accounts`, which does not conflict with a reader or a foreign-key check. This also matches DB-AUTH-001 ("assignments remain separate relations") and leaves `app.user_accounts` and its column test unchanged. As built: (1) `app.user_account_classes` (`actor_id` primary key and foreign key to `app.user_accounts`, ON UPDATE and ON DELETE RESTRICT; `account_class` NOT NULL, one of the three; `classified_at`; non-blank `provenance`); (2) partial unique index `user_account_classes_single_owner` (at most one `owner`); (3) trigger function `app.reject_user_account_class_change()` on BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE (each row) and BEFORE TRUNCATE: a class, once given, never changes or goes away (23000, "user account class is immutable"); (4) `app.require_user_account_class_mfa()` BEFORE INSERT: an `owner` or `manager` class needs the account's `mfa_policy_class` `required`, read with a share lock on the account row so a concurrent MFA change is waited for and seen (23514, "an Owner or Manager account requires MFA"); (5) `app.reject_privileged_account_optional_mfa()` AFTER UPDATE on `app.user_accounts`, for each row whose new MFA policy is not `required` (review round 1: AFTER, so it checks the final row): the same message when an `owner` or `manager` account's MFA would stop being required, and (security review round 1, fail closed) any change of an MFA policy to a value other than `required` is refused outside READ COMMITTED (55000), because the class check could read an older snapshot; (6) the three trigger functions are not definers, have `search_path=pg_catalog` and no EXECUTE for PUBLIC; (7) backfill: one `owner` row for the closure's actor (`login-slice-account-class-backfill`), no other row, `app.user_accounts` untouched; (8) `prm_runtime` gets SELECT on the new relation only; (9) the bootstrap function inserts the `owner` class row right after the account row (one exact-text change; same signature, owner, ACL, definer flag and settings). A class can be given only by the migration owner or a definer function; an old unclassified account is never classified by any function: the Owner disables it and creates a new account (Q-152 answer).
  - Review round 1 (no blocker; should-fixes are tests and fail-closed refusals): the race tests in both orders and the READ COMMITTED refusal (both isolation levels) are added; the backfill test also checks that a bootstrap closed before the upgrade stays closed; the sign-in unit test also checks the class join (stricter); text fixes. Notes kept for later sub-slices: L2's account create refuses `owner` and records who gave the class (SEC-075); L4 decides a class check in `app.perform_account_recovery`; L1b, L2 and L3a keep the invariant that every authority path joins the class; L7 runbook: never run the bootstrap while a migration runs, and if a bootstrap ever closes without an Owner class, recovery needs a reviewed forward migration that inserts the `owner` class (with MFA `required`). Review round 2 (no blocker, no should-fix; one combined reviewer for both checklists): notes taken: the share-lock comment now says the wait-and-see holds at READ COMMITTED and a newer MFA change fails the lock at REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE, with a new test; for the L7 runbook: the backfill refuses (23514) if the closure's actor no longer requires MFA; this stale Tests line marked. Notes kept: READ UNCOMMITTED is refused too (PostgreSQL runs it as READ COMMITTED; fail closed); ad-hoc pytest runs on a long-lived database upgraded from 174 with a committed test closure would leave an Owner there (the scripts use a fresh database). `administrative_recovery.py` needs no change: it already refuses class labels outside the three, which now come from the resolver.
  - Code: `account_recovery.py` gains `PostgresRecoveryAccountResolver` (reads the stored class of an active, classified account; the request's class labels stay ignored), and the `TrustedAccountRecoveryAuthorizer` docstring no longer says the schema has no class relation; `local_authentication.py` as above. `initial_owner_bootstrap.py` is not changed (same function signature). `app.perform_account_recovery` is not changed in L1a (L4 decides whether it checks the classes again).
  - Committed tests changed: the head-revision strings only (27 in 15 modules).
  - New tests (`test_account_class_migration.py`, last in `scripts/database-test.sh`): the class values, one class per account, the foreign key; Owner and Manager need required MFA (class insert and later MFA change); at most one Owner; a class never changes or goes away (update, delete, truncate); the bootstrapped Owner has class `owner` and a second Owner is refused (TEST-133, TEST-134); the backfill classes only the bootstrapped actor and leaves `app.user_accounts` unchanged; the recovery resolver reads the stored class (TEST-130); an account without a class cannot be found for sign-in while a classified one can; least privilege and forward-only (only the bootstrap function body changes, by exactly the class insert; three functions, four triggers, one relation with its indexes, constraints and columns added; `prm_runtime` gets SELECT on the new relation only).

#### L1b — Capability catalog, bundles and assignments (tables only)
- Builds: `app.capabilities` (catalog: id, family, description, `assignable_by_bundle` flag; replaced in L1b-1 by a `grant_path`: `bundle`, `per_user`, `owner_class` or `service_principal`), seeded with every capability the code checks today plus the new names approved under Q-151, Q-158 and Q-160; `app.role_bundles` (per Property, name unique per Property, version), `app.role_bundle_capabilities`, `app.user_role_assignments` (append-only history: assigned and removed events, never updated in place); a check that `billing.generate` and `settings.manage` can never be put in a bundle (changed by Q-2026-10-21-161 (a) and Q-2026-10-21-162 (b): only capabilities whose catalog grant path is `bundle` can be put in a bundle; `settings.manage` is per user, `identity.manage_access` Owner class only, `rent_nonpayment.evaluate` a service principal's; `billing.generate` is a bundle capability); a read function `app.actor_capability_grants(actor_id)` (SECURITY DEFINER, fixed `search_path`) that returns the effective capabilities with their Property ids for an active, classified account. A code test compares the catalog with every capability constant in `backend/src`, so a new constant without a catalog row fails.
- Rules: SEC-001 to SEC-003, SEC-020, SEC-021, SEC-022, SEC-014, API-080, DB-AUTH-001 (assignments are separate relations), TEST-084, TEST-086.
- Files: new migration; new `access_control.py` (catalog constants and the grant reader); docs/004 (new section after DB-AUTH-005, for example DB-AUTH-006 to DB-AUTH-008); docs/008 note under SEC-021.
- Tests: migration tests (tables, uniqueness, append-only assignments, the two never-in-a-bundle capabilities refused (changed by L1b-1, Q-161 (a) and Q-162 (b): every capability whose grant path is not `bundle` refused, that is `settings.manage` (per_user), `identity.manage_access` (owner_class) and `rent_nonpayment.evaluate` (service_principal)), grants of a disabled or unclassified account are empty, least privilege of `prm_runtime`, forward-only); the catalog-matches-code test.
- Risks: a capability string used only inside a database function (for example audit labels such as `exchange_rates.manage` in migration `20260825_18`) must keep its exact spelling; the catalog adds names, it renames nothing.
- Split (implementer's, allowed by the owner's instruction of 2026-10-21): L1b-1, the capability catalog; L1b-2, role bundles, assignments and the grant reader.
- L1b-1 pre-code design (2026-10-21; read-only survey of every dotted string literal in `backend/src` and in the migrations): 71 capabilities exist today: 70 checked in `backend/src` (for example `financial.approve`, `final_settlements.prepare`, `late_payment.final_decision`, `late_payment.charge_correction`) and `rent_nonpayment.evaluate`, checked only by the database (the nonpayment evaluation principal, migration `20260910_51`); every other dotted literal is a request-digest, audit-action, log-event or function label (for example `lease.sign`, `deposit.security.create`, `reservation.extend`). The catalog adds the four approved names `settings.manage` (Q-151), `operations.status.read` (Q-158), `property.read` and `units.read` (Q-160): 75 rows. Migration `20270119_176` (additive): `app.capabilities` (`capability_id` key, lower-case dotted form checked; `family` = the part before the first dot, checked; non-blank `description`; `assignable_by_bundle`; `added_at`; non-blank `provenance`), seeded with the 75 rows; `assignable_by_bundle` is false for `billing.generate` and `rent_nonpayment.evaluate` (service principals) and `settings.manage` (per user only, Q-151), true for the rest (replaced in review round 1, security should-fix S1, Q-161 (a) and Q-162 (b): a `grant_path` column, `bundle`, `per_user` (`settings.manage`), `owner_class` (`identity.manage_access`) or `service_principal` (`rent_nonpayment.evaluate`), with `UNIQUE (capability_id, grant_path)` for the L1b-2 bundle reference; `billing.generate` is `bundle`, its description "Start a Rent or Utility billing run and read its status"; a name at most 128 characters; a finite `added_at`; the unit test also checks the constants of `access_control.py` and uses `fullmatch`); a new trigger function `app.reject_capability_catalog_change()` (no grant, `search_path=pg_catalog`) refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE (23000, "capability catalog is append-only"); `prm_runtime` gets SELECT (the API-080 capability list). No other object changes. Code: new `access_control.py` with `CAPABILITY_CATALOG` (id to description), the grant path sets `PER_USER_CAPABILITIES`, `OWNER_CLASS_CAPABILITIES` and `SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_CAPABILITIES`, `capability_grant_path` (an unknown name refused), `BUNDLE_CAPABILITIES` (72) and constants for the new names and `identity.manage_access`. Tests: unit `test_access_control.py` (every dotted string constant in `backend/src` is a catalog capability or one of the listed non-capability labels, so a new capability without a catalog row fails; every dotted constant of `access_control.py` is a catalog name; the four new names are in the catalog; each capability has one grant path, the three sets do not overlap); PostgreSQL `test_capability_catalog_migration.py` (the table equals `CAPABILITY_CATALOG` and each grant path; the format and family checks; append-only; least privilege and forward-only).
- L1b-2 pre-code design (2026-10-21, fresh session; read-only survey of `20260817_02`, `20260823_13` (the single Property, `app.properties.id`, one row by `singleton_key`), `20270118_175`, `20270119_176`, `identity.py`, `access_admin_api.py` (API-080 shapes: a bundle has an id, a Property, a name, capability ids and a version; an assignment names a user, a bundle and the Property), `local_authentication.py` and `account_recovery.py`): migration `20270120_177` (additive; new relations, functions and triggers only; the new foreign keys take SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on `app.properties`, `app.user_accounts` and `app.capabilities`, as in L1a). (1) `app.role_bundles`, the current state of a bundle: `role_bundle_id` (key), `property_id` (foreign key to `app.properties`, RESTRICT), `name` (trimmed, 1 to 128 characters, `UNIQUE (property_id, name)`), `version` (from 1), finite `created_at`, non-blank `provenance`, and `UNIQUE (role_bundle_id, property_id)` for the assignment reference; a new bundle starts at version 1; an update may change only the name and must raise the version by exactly 1 (23000, "a role bundle changes only its name and its next version"); never deleted or truncated. (2) `app.role_bundle_versions`, append-only history: one row (`role_bundle_id`, `version`, `name`, `recorded_at`, `recorded_transaction` = the writing transaction's id) written by an AFTER trigger for every new bundle and every update; a hand-written row that is not the bundle's current version and name is refused (23000, "a role bundle version is written only with its bundle"). (3) `app.role_bundle_capabilities`, append-only, the complete capability set of each version: (`role_bundle_id`, `version`, `capability_id`), a `grant_path` that must be `bundle`, foreign keys to the version and to `app.capabilities (capability_id, grant_path)`, so `settings.manage`, `identity.manage_access`, `rent_nonpayment.evaluate` and unknown names can never be in a bundle (Q-161 (a), Q-162 (b)); rows are written only for the bundle's current version and only in the transaction that wrote that version (23000, "role bundle capabilities are written only with their version"), so a recorded version never changes; the current set is the rows of the bundle's current version. (4) `app.user_role_assignments`, append-only: `assignment_id`, `actor_id` (foreign key to `app.user_accounts`), `role_bundle_id` and `property_id` (foreign key to the bundle and its Property together), finite `assigned_at`, `assigned_by_actor_id` (null for seeds), non-blank `provenance`; at most one active assignment of a bundle to an account, checked under a per-account-and-bundle advisory lock at READ COMMITTED only (23505, "a role bundle is already assigned to this account"; 55000 outside READ COMMITTED, the L1a fail-closed reason). (5) `app.user_role_assignment_removals`, append-only: `assignment_id` (key and foreign key, so an assignment is removed at most once), finite `removed_at`, `removed_by_actor_id`, non-blank `reason` and `provenance`; an assignment is active while it has no removal. (6) Every UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on the four history relations, and DELETE and TRUNCATE on `app.role_bundles`, are refused (23000, "role bundle history is append-only"). #### L1d — Per-user Settings access (needs Q-2026-10-21-151)

Removing it revokes nothing else and takes effect at the next request.

(1) `app.user_capability_grants`, append-only: `grant_id` (key), `actor_id` (foreign key to `app.user_accounts`), `capability_id` with `grant_path` `per_user` (a check allows only `settings.manage` and `per_user`; a foreign key on both to `app.capabilities`), finite `given_at`, `given_by_actor_id` (not null, foreign key to `app.user_accounts`), a non-blank `reason` and `provenance` of at most 500 characters; at most one active grant of a capability to an account, checked under a per-account advisory lock at READ COMMITTED only (23505, "this account already has Settings access"; 55000 outside READ COMMITTED). (2) `app.user_capability_grant_removals`, append-only: `grant_id` (key and foreign key, so a grant ends at most once), finite `removed_at`, `removed_by_actor_id` (not null, foreign key), reason and provenance as above. (3) UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE refused on both (23000, "settings access history is append-only"). (4) Definer functions `app.give_settings_access(p_owner_id uuid, p_actor_id uuid, p_reason text)` and `app.remove_settings_access(p_owner_id uuid, p_actor_id uuid, p_reason text)` (`search_path=pg_catalog`): the acting account must be active with class `owner` (42501, "only the Owner gives or removes Settings access"); the target must be active and classed `manager` or `staff` (22023, "Settings access is given only to a Manager or Staff account"; the Owner always has it); give refuses an account that already has it (the trigger), remove refuses one that has none (55000, "this account has no Settings access"); each returns the grant id; `prm_runtime` may execute both (L2's routes call them; the routes add the reauthentication of Q-157). Tests: PostgreSQL `test_settings_access_migration.py` (last in `scripts/database-test.sh`): the Owner gives and removes; a Manager, a Staff member, a disabled or unclassified acting account cannot; an Owner, disabled or unclassified target cannot get it; give twice and remove without a grant are refused; give again after a removal; only `settings.manage` can be stored; append-only; the reader (Owner always, a given Manager or Staff account, gone at the next read after removal, a disabled holder gets nothing); a waiting-thread race of two gives; least privilege and forward-only. #### L1e — Settings access needs the sign-in code (owner rule of 2026-10-21; DL-081, amends DL-074 answer 2)
- Owner rule (recorded in commit 88d5bfd): any account that holds Settings access must use the sign-in code (MFA) at every sign-in, like the Owner and Manager classes; the Owner can give Settings access to a Staff account only after that account has set up its sign-in code, otherwise the give is refused with a plain message; no path may leave a Staff account with Settings access and no sign-in code. Placed here (a small sub-slice after L1d and L1c) because the give function and the reader exist and the sign-in code table (`app.totp_mfa_enrollments`, migration `20260819_06`) already records a set-up code; the reset and MFA-off paths are built later (L2, L3c, L4) and wait for Q-2026-10-21-165.
- L1e pre-code design (2026-10-21, same session; read-only survey of `20260819_06` (an enrollment is `pending`, `active` or `disabled`; at most one live per account; the account recovery of `20260819_08` disables the live enrollment when it resets MFA), `20270121_178`, the L1d tests): migration `20270123_180` (both functions replaced with the same signature, owner, privileges and attributes, and one new internal function `app.staff_sign_in_code_is_set_up(actor)` that both use: STABLE, not a definer, `search_path=pg_catalog`, no EXECUTE for PUBLIC or the runtime role; nothing else). (1) `app.give_settings_access`: after the Owner and target checks, a Staff target must have MFA policy `required` and an `active` sign-in code enrollment, otherwise 55000 "a Staff account gets Settings access only after it has set up its sign-in code". A Manager target is not checked here: the Manager class always requires the sign-in code (L1a), and no session gets an actor before it is done (L3c). (2) The reader `app.actor_capability_grants`: a per-user grant gives `settings.manage` to a Manager, and to a Staff account only while its MFA policy is `required` and it has an `active` enrollment; so a code reset, a lowered MFA policy, a hand-written grant or a give that raced a reset gives nothing, whatever path caused it (fail closed; this is the guarantee behind "no path may leave"). The Owner class is unchanged. (3) Q-2026-10-21-165 asks what a reset or MFA-off path does to the grant row itself (recommendation: remove it in the same step); until the answer, the grant stays recorded but gives nothing. (4) The reader checks the account, not the session (review round 1, should-fix 2): a Staff session started while the account's MFA policy was `optional` never used the code. Binding for L2 and L3c: when a Staff account's MFA policy is raised to `required`, its sessions are revoked in the same transaction (L2 test: a committed Staff session with `optional` policy is revoked when the policy is set to `required` through the L2 path), and L3c gives a Staff account with MFA `required` an actor only after the code at every sign-in. Notes for L2: the give raises 55000 for two reasons ("Settings access is given only at READ COMMITTED" and the sign-in code message), so the route tells them apart by message. Note for L3c: `active` is only as trustworthy as the L3c check of a correct code before the runtime role activates an enrollment. Committed tests changed (new refusal and committed set-ups, the run rule of 2026-10-19): `test_settings_access_migration.py::test_the_owner_gives_and_removes_settings_access` and `::test_the_reader_gives_settings_access_to_the_owner_and_to_given_accounts_only` first assert that the give to the Staff account without a sign-in code is refused, then give the account a sign-in code and give again, with every check kept; `::test_the_runtime_role_reaches_settings_access_only_through_its_functions` gives its committed Staff holder a committed sign-in code in its set-up; a new helper `add_sign_in_code` (MFA policy `required`, an enrollment written as the table owner and activated) sits in that module. Tests (new module `test_settings_access_sign_in_code_migration.py`, last in `scripts/database-test.sh`): the give refuses a Staff account with no code, a pending code, or an active code with MFA policy `optional`, and accepts it with both; a Manager without a code can be given it; the reader gives a Staff holder nothing after its code is disabled, after its MFA policy is lowered, or for a hand-written grant without a code, and gives it again after a new code is set up; least privilege and forward-only (only the two function bodies change and the internal function is added). Head-revision assertions move to `20270123_180` (27 in 15 modules). Docs: docs/004 DB-AUTH-008 note, docs/008 SEC-013 and SEC-021 notes, docs/010 DL-081 lines, traceability appended, the new question.

#### L2 — Account and bundle administration on PostgreSQL (needs Q-152, Q-153, Q-157)
- Builds: `PostgresAccessAdministrationFlow` for the existing API-079 and API-080 routes: list and create users (create takes `account_class` `manager` or `staff`; the MFA policy follows the class; the default bundle of that class is assigned at creation, as Q-152 answers), update and disable (disable revokes every session), revoke sessions, capability list from the catalog, bundle list, create and update (refuses `settings.manage` and `billing.generate`; changed by Q-2026-10-21-161 (a) and Q-2026-10-21-162 (b): refuses every capability whose grant path is not `bundle`, that is `settings.manage`, `identity.manage_access` and `rent_nonpayment.evaluate`), assignment, authorization history; two new routes for Settings access (proposed `POST /users/{user_id}/settings-access` and `POST /users/{user_id}/settings-access/remove`, each with a reason). Every action writes an audit event without secrets (SEC-014, SEC-075). The resolver fills the object scopes the existing route checks need (`user_account` and `role_bundle` ids of the Property) for holders of `identity.manage_access` (by Q-2026-10-21-162 (b), the Owner account class only). High-risk actions require recent reauthentication as Q-157 answers. Raising a Staff account's MFA policy to `required` revokes its sessions in the same transaction, with a test (L1e point 4); what a sign-in code reset or MFA off does to Settings access waits for Q-2026-10-21-165.
- Rules: API-079, API-080, SEC-014, SEC-017, SEC-018, SEC-021, SEC-075, DL-074 answers 1 and 2.
- Files: `access_admin_api.py` (new request field `account_class`, the two Settings access routes), new `access_admin_flow.py`, `app.py` wiring; docs/005 API-079 and API-080 (new routes listed; they need the owner's yes, Q-158).
- Tests: route and flow tests for each action, allowed and denied (missing capability, wrong Property, disabled account, revoked session), audit evidence, no credential in any response (TEST-084, TEST-085, TEST-110).
- Risks: the existing route tests use the unavailable flow and fakes; they keep working because injection stays.
- Split (implementer's, allowed by the owner's instruction of 2026-10-21): L2a, the administration functions in the database (one migration and its PostgreSQL tests); L2b, the Python flow `PostgresAccessAdministrationFlow`, the API changes, the two Settings access routes, the object scopes, the `create_app` wiring and the frontend client type change. Reauthentication (Q-157) is added to these routes by L3d, which builds the check; no L2 route is reachable before L3a, and no build between L3a and L5 is used. The Owner's reset stays unavailable in the Postgres flow until L4.
- L2a pre-code design (2026-10-21, fresh session, after the owner's answer (a) to Q-2026-10-21-165; read-only survey of `20260817_02` (`app.user_accounts`: no version column; `prm_runtime` SELECT only), `20260819_07` (`app.browser_sessions`: revocation by UPDATE of `revoked_by_actor_id`, `revocation_reason` (one of `logout`, `password_reset`, `mfa_reset`, `mfa_recovery`, `account_disabled`, `material_privilege_reduction`) and `revocation_provenance`; the trigger sets `revoked_at`), `20260823_10` (`app.audit_events`, append-only; `prm_runtime` SELECT and INSERT), `20260827_29` (a trigger adds the HUMAN actor identity for every new account), `20270118_175` to `20270123_180`, `access_admin_api.py` (API-079 and API-080 shapes: an account has a version used with If-Match; no route removes an assignment) and the L1 tests): migration `20270124_181` (additive: new relations, functions and grants only; nothing existing is altered, because adding a column to `app.user_accounts` deadlocks the V1-042 upgrade test, L1a design change 2). (1) `app.user_account_changes`, append-only: one row per administrative change of an account (`actor_id`, `version` from 2, unique per account, `changed_at`, `changed_by_actor_id` (an account), `change_kind`, non-secret `previous_state` and `resulting_state`, provenance); an account's version is 1 plus its number of change rows (accounts made before L2 start at 1). #### L2d — Tidy spaces in names and at sign-in (owner answer Q-2026-10-22-170 (a), 2026-10-22)
- Placed in its own small sub-slice before L3a (implementer's choice, as the owner allowed): it changes the same name, username and sign-in lookup steps as L2c, and L3a then builds the sign-in on the finished username rule.
- Pre-code design (2026-10-22, fresh session; read-only survey of `visible_text.py`, `access_admin_api.py` (`BoundedName`), `access_admin_flow.py` (`SPACE_SEPARATORS`, `normalized_name`, `normalized_username`), `local_authentication.py` (`normalize_local_username` and its two callers, the sign-in lookup and the attempt limiter key), the account form in `frontend/src/App.tsx` (it only checks that the display name is not blank and trims it, so nothing changes on the screen) and the tests that hold odd spaces): (1) `visible_text.py` gets `SPACE_SEPARATORS` (moved from the flow: the Unicode space separators, category Zs) and `tidy_spaces` (each run of them becomes one U+0020, none at either end). Tabs, line breaks and other control characters are not spaces: they are not changed and stay refused (decided by Claude Code under the owner's 2026-10-22 rule: a tab or line break in a name is a paste mistake, and the database refuses it). (2) API: `BoundedName` removes U+200B and tidies spaces before the trim and the length rule, so the 128 limit counts the characters that are saved. (3) Flow: `normalized_name` uses `tidy_spaces` (the same result as today); `normalized_username` is `normalize_local_username` followed by a refusal of any white space left that is not U+0020 (a tab or a line break), so a username typed with a no-break space, a thin space, an ideographic space or two spaces in a row is saved with one ordinary space instead of being refused. (4) Sign-in: `normalize_local_username` removes U+200B, makes the username NFC, tidies spaces and makes it lower case; the lookup and the wrong-try key use it, so "Sokha  Chan", "Sokha" + U+00A0 + "Chan" and " sokha chan " all find and count the account "sokha chan". (5) Database: nothing changes; the L2c name checks stay the last guard (a direct write with two spaces in a row is still refused, as L2c tests). No migration. (6) Frontend: nothing changes; the screen refuses no space. (7) Tests: unit (`test_local_authentication.py`) the lookup and the limiter key tidy spaces; (`test_access_admin_flow.py`) a username with odd and double spaces is saved with one ordinary space and a tab or line break is still refused; (`test_access_admin_api.py`) a username, display name and audit name with odd and double spaces reach the flow tidied, and the 128 limit counts the tidied name; PostgreSQL (`test_name_hidden_characters_migration.py`, already in the full-run list) the owner's example: "Sokha  Chan" typed twice with two spaces is saved as the display name "Sokha Chan" and the username "sokha chan", every typed spelling looks up that username, and the same username typed with a no-break space is taken. Committed tests changed: the owner answer changes the result of `test_access_admin_flow.py::test_names_are_nfc_with_single_spaces_and_usernames_lower_case` (the usernames with U+00A0, U+2009 and U+3000 are now saved as "ann lee"; "ann" + tab + "lee" stays refused; its traceability note changes); `test_name_hidden_characters_migration.py` imports `SPACE_SEPARATORS` from `visible_text`. Docs: docs/005 API-080 and API-096 notes, the DL-081 L2d line, NOW.md.

#### L3a — Password sign-in, server-side sessions, actor resolver and sign-out
- Builds: `PostgresAuthenticationFlow.login` (calls `LocalAuthenticationService`, then creates an `app.browser_sessions` row with a random 32-byte token whose sha256 verifier is stored; the token goes only into the `__Host-prm_session` cookie; a new CSRF token on every sign-in), `inspect_session` (adds `display_name` to `SessionView` so the shell can show the name), `logout` (revokes the row, clears the cookies); `PostgresSessionActorResolver` (section 7.2); `create_app` wiring when a database is configured; the session read and activity update in one short transaction per request. An Owner or Manager account in this sub-slice gets only the "MFA required" phase (no actor) until L3c, so nothing privileged is reachable without MFA at any commit.
- Rules: DL-055, DL-057, API-008, API-096, API-097, SEC-008 to SEC-011, SEC-015 to SEC-017, SEC-023, SEC-030, DB-AUTH-002, DB-AUTH-004, UI-111.
- Files: new `auth_flow.py` and `session_actor.py`; `auth_api.py` (`SessionView.display_name`), `app.py`, `local_authentication.py` (repository also reads class and display name); possibly an additive migration for runtime grants the flow needs (to be confirmed by a read-only check of the existing grants first); docs/005 API-096 and API-097 notes.
- Tests: sign-in with a correct password (Staff without MFA), wrong password, unknown user, disabled user, unclassified user, all with the same 401 body and similar timing; the session cookie flags (`Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`, `__Host-`, path `/`), token never in logs or URLs; idle expiry right after 30 minutes and absolute expiry after 24 hours with a controlled database clock; logout; a revoked or expired session gives 401 on a protected route; the resolver gives exactly the bundle grants; a capability removed from a bundle is refused at the next request (TEST-108, TEST-110, TEST-131, TEST-135).
- Ordering rule (L1c review round 2): until L5 is committed, the rate routes check `service_rates.manage` and `utility_rates.manage`, and the Property update, Property configuration and due-days setting check `property.manage`; all are in the default Manager bundle, so a build with the L3a resolver and without L5 is never used.
- Risks: the per-request database read adds a little latency (fine at under 100 Units); the clock for expiry is the database clock, as for the financial fixtures.
- Pre-code design (2026-10-23, same session as L2d; read-only survey of `auth_api.py` (the `AuthenticationFlow` protocol, the routes, the cookie rules), `local_authentication.py`, `browser_session.py`, migration `20260819_07` (`app.browser_sessions`: sha256 verifier, database-clock timestamps, the activity and revocation trigger, the runtime role's column grants: SELECT, INSERT of `session_id`, `actor_id`, `token_verifier`, `verifier_algorithm`, `creation_provenance`, UPDATE of `last_activity_at` and the revocation columns), `access_control.py` (`PostgresCapabilityGrantReader`), `access_admin_flow.py` (the scope reader), `api.py` (`/identity/me` needs `identity.read_self` with the `actor` object scope), `app.py` (`create_app`, the 429 and 503 handlers), the audit table (it needs a Property, which does not exist when the Owner first signs in) and the frontend session read (the shell reads the session once and times expiry from `idle_expires_at`)). Split into two commits (implementer's choice, as the owner allowed):
  - L3a-1, sign-in, the session read and sign-out (`auth_flow.py`, no migration: the runtime role already has every grant it needs): `PostgresAuthenticationFlow(database_url)` implements `login`, `inspect_session` and `logout`; the MFA, enrollment, reauthentication and recovery-code methods stay unavailable (503) until L3c and L3d. `login` uses the existing `LocalAuthenticationService` (dummy verifier for unknown names, one generic rejection, Argon2id through `PasswordHashService`), built once per flow with a lookup that opens its own short connection per call (sign-in requests run in parallel threads), and the existing in-memory limiter as a coarse per-process flood guard (20 tries per username and 100 per source in 15 minutes; decided by Claude Code under the owner's 2026-10-22 rule; L3b adds the database count of 5 wrong tries). Every rejection (wrong password, unknown, disabled or unclassified account, the flood guard) answers the same 401. An account whose MFA policy is `required` (Owner, Manager, Staff with MFA) gets the phase `mfa_required` with a random pre-authentication token that is not stored, and no session and no actor; the challenge answers unavailable until L3c builds the stored pre-authentication state and the enrollment phase. An account whose MFA policy is `optional` gets a session: a random 32-byte token (`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, standard library) goes only into the `__Host-prm_session` cookie; the database stores only its sha256 digest (`hashlib`), with provenance `auth-login`; a new random CSRF token on every sign-in. `SessionView` and the API's `SessionData` gain `display_name` (read from the account in the same transaction). `inspect_session` finds the session by the digest of the cookie and answers it only while it is not revoked, the database clock is before both `idle_expires_at` and `absolute_expires_at`, and the account is active, classified and has MFA policy `optional` (until L3c adds the MFA proof); otherwise the generic 401. It records no activity (decided by Claude Code under the owner's 2026-10-22 rule: the shell reads the session to time its expiry, and a read of the session must not keep an idle session alive). `logout` revokes the session found by the digest when it is not revoked and before both expiries, whatever the account's state (reason `logout`, revoked by its own account, provenance `auth-logout`; review round 3 wording) and the route clears the three cookies; an unknown, revoked or expired session gives the generic 401. A cookie value longer than 128 characters is refused before hashing. No password, token, digest or username is logged; the session rows keep who signed in when and who ended the session when and why (no audit event, because the audit table needs a Property; L3b's failed-try table records the refusals). `create_app` uses `PostgresAuthenticationFlow` when `APP_DATABASE_URL` is set and no flow is given; `LoginRequest.username` is narrowed from 256 to 128 characters (the longest saved username; L2c note), so NFC never runs on a long input.
  - L3a-2, the actor resolver and its wiring (`session_actor.py`): `PostgresSessionActorResolver(database_url)` reads the session cookie on every request and, in one short READ COMMITTED transaction, finds the live session as `inspect_session` does, records the activity (`UPDATE ... SET last_activity_at = statement_timestamp()` guarded by `last_activity_at < statement_timestamp()`, so two parallel requests never trip the trigger; the trigger sets the new idle expiry, never past the absolute one), reads the grants through `PostgresCapabilityGrantReader` (fresh on every request, so a removed capability or bundle stops at the next request), adds the Owner's object scopes to `identity.manage_access` (`with_administration_scopes` and `PostgresAccessAdministrationScopeReader`) and the `actor` scope of the actor itself to `identity.read_self`, and returns the `AuthenticatedActor`; no cookie, an unknown, revoked or expired session, or an account that is disabled, unclassified or has MFA policy `required` gives no actor (401); a database error answers 503 (fail closed). `create_app` uses it when `APP_DATABASE_URL` is set and no resolver is given (building it opens no connection); tests keep injecting their own. Ordering rule (L1c): no build between L3a and L5 is used.
  - Tests, L3a-1: PostgreSQL `test_auth_flow_migration.py` (last in `scripts/database-test.sh`; one throwaway database at head; accounts and real Argon2id credentials written as the table owner): a Staff account signs in (session row with the sha256 digest of the cookie token and never the token, display name in the view, CSRF token), reads its session and signs out (revoked by itself with reason `logout`; reading or signing out again gives 401); a wrong password, an unknown username, a disabled account and an unclassified account all give the same rejection and write no session; an Owner and a Manager get `mfa_required` with no session; idle expiry (a session last active 29 minutes ago is read, 31 minutes ago is refused) and absolute expiry (created 24 hours ago, last active 10 minutes ago, refused), with session rows written as the table owner from the database clock; the HTTP routes through `create_app` with the real flow (cookie names, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, path `/`, no `Domain`, the token never in the body, `Cache-Control: no-store`, the same 401 body for every rejection) and no token, password or username in the logs. Unit: the narrowed `LoginRequest`, the cookie length bound, the unavailable MFA methods. L3a-2: PostgreSQL `test_session_actor_migration.py` (last in the full-run list): the resolver gives exactly the account's bundle grants (and the Owner's class capabilities and scopes), records activity, refuses a revoked, expired, disabled or MFA-required session, and a capability removed from the account's bundle is refused at the next request; a protected route answers 401 without or after the session (TEST-108, TEST-110, TEST-131, TEST-135).
  - Security checklist (the security-and-hardening skill, as the owner asked): trust boundary is the HTTP request (username, password, cookies, Origin, CSRF header); assets are the password verifier, the session token and the grants; spoofing (Argon2id, sha256 token digest, unique random token), tampering (parameterized SQL only), repudiation (session rows), information disclosure (one 401 body, no secrets in logs or responses, `no-store`), denial of service (bounded inputs, the flood guard now and the database count in L3b), elevation of privilege (grants read fresh from the database on every request; no actor before MFA where it is required).
  - As built after review round 1 (one independent and one security agent; no blocker; U1, T1 and P1 of the first build passed first): the session transaction checks the password again against the current verifier (a reset that committed after the first check leaves no session with the old password); a 5-second connect timeout on every connection; new tests: a session refused after its account is disabled or its MFA policy raised, an unreachable database answers 503, the flood guard (20 tries per username, 100 per source); the first database test compares only its own rows; the unit test no longer claims that no connection is opened; docs/005 API-097 names the MFA policy condition. Binding for L4: a reset and a racing session write must not both commit (the remaining gap between the second check and the commit). Note for L3b and L7: the source key is the connecting address; behind a reverse proxy every person would share one source. Review round 2 (one fresh agent, both checklists; after U2 and P2): no blocker; one text should-fix done (the L4 binding now names every password or MFA replacement); notes taken as text: binding for L3c, a session is made, and read, only for an account with no active sign-in code enrollment unless the MFA challenge was completed (an `optional` account with an active enrollment must complete MFA, DL-056); a pointer under docs/005 API-096. Notes kept: the 128-character sign-in limit applies before tidying (a 128-character username typed with an extra space gets 422, rare); the absolute-expiry condition cannot be tested apart from the idle one (the table caps idle at absolute); an optional extra verifier read just before the commit would shrink the L4 gap further; no statement timeout yet (L3a-2). Review round 3 (one fresh agent, both checklists): no blocker; one text should-fix done (sign-out revokes a session that is not revoked and before both expiries, whatever the account's state, in docs/005, DL-081 and this plan); text notes done (a test docstring, a flow docstring, docs/005 precision). Binding for L3a-2 (round 3 note): logout's `statement_timestamp()` is taken when its statement starts, so an activity update with a later time that commits first could make the revocation break `CHECK (revoked_at >= last_activity_at)` and answer 503; L3a-2 handles it (for example logout retries once, or refuses only after re-reading) and tests a logout racing an activity update. Notes kept: signing in again does not revoke an older session; the in-memory limiter never forgets keys (L3b).
  - L3a-2 as built (2026-10-23, same session): `session_actor.py` as designed; the activity is written first and the live session read after it in the same transaction (a revocation or expiry meanwhile gives no actor); a 5-second statement timeout on every connection of the flow and the resolver (L3a-1 review round 2 note); a capability removed from a bundle revokes its holders' sessions (L2a), so the test of the fresh grant read gives a bundle and then removes it. Tests: PostgreSQL `test_session_actor_migration.py` (3, last in the full-run list), unit `test_session_actor.py` (2). As built after review round 1 (one independent and one security agent; U1, T1 and P1 of the first build passed first): the security agent's blocker (every Owner revocation, and sign-out, could roll back with a check violation when the person's own request committed a later activity, so a person who kept using the app could stop their own revocation) is fixed at its root by migration `20270127_184` (relaxing): `app.protect_browser_session_lifecycle` records `GREATEST(statement time, last activity)` as the revocation time (design change under the design-change run rule, for the round 2 reviewers to confirm); the planned sign-out guard and second statement are removed; the activity is recorded only for a session of an active, classified account with MFA policy `optional`; the Owner's scope read has the connect and statement timeouts; new tests: a sign-out and an Owner revocation that each wait for the session row while a later activity commits (`test_session_revocation_time_migration.py`, with the migration's least-privilege and forward-only checks; the reviewer's set-up: hold the row `FOR UPDATE` as the table owner, start the revocation in a thread, wait until `pg_locks` shows an ungranted lock in the database (`pg_stat_activity` hides another role's wait from a role that is not a superuser; found by run T2), record the activity, commit), the Owner branch and a catalog mismatch with stand-ins (`test_session_actor.py`), 401 after sign-out on a protected route; the 27 head-revision strings in 15 modules. Review round 2 (one fresh agent, both checklists; after U2 and P2): no blocker; the trigger design change confirmed as needed and safe, and the race tests confirmed to reproduce the failing order; three should-fix, done: the DL-081 L3a-2 line no longer says "no migration" (text), both race tests assert that the revocation time equals the last activity (test), and the refused sessions are checked to get no activity (test); the forward-only test's docstring no longer claims an owner and privilege check it does not make (text). Review round 3 (one fresh agent, both checklists; after U3 and P3): no blocker; one text should-fix done (the DL-081 line records the round 2 confirmation and tests). #### L3b — Wrong-try limit: 5 tries, 15-minute wait (needs Q-2026-10-21-154)
- Builds: an append-only table of failed sign-in tries keyed by the normalized username and, separately, by the request source; `LocalAuthenticationService` checks the wait before checking the password, counts only wrong tries, and after the 5th wrong try for a username refuses every try for 15 minutes with the one wait message, whether or not the account exists (unknown usernames are counted the same way). The in-memory `BoundedAuthenticationAttemptLimiter` stays as a coarse per-process flood guard. Wrong MFA codes and wrong recovery codes count as wrong tries (as Q-154 answers). Every refusal is audited without the password.
- Rules: DL-080 item 10, SEC-012, UI-109, API-096, API-098, SEC-071.
- Files: new migration; `local_authentication.py`; `auth_flow.py`; `auth_api.py` (the wait answer: proposed 429 with one fixed message and no account detail); docs/005 API-096 note, docs/008 SEC-012 already amended.
- Tests: tries 1 to 4 wrong then a correct one succeeds; 5 wrong tries then the correct password is refused for 15 minutes and accepted just after; the same body for an existing and an unknown username; the wait does not grow with tries during it (as Q-154 answers); a restart (new service object) keeps the count; the source bound; no password or username text in logs (TEST-108, TEST-129, TEST-110).
- Risks: anyone who knows a username can make that person wait 15 minutes (also the Owner); the Owner then waits or uses the emergency server procedure (DL-058). Q-154 asks whether that is acceptable.
- Owner rule amendment (given by the owner on 2026-10-23 in the session message, as the rule amended on 2026-10-21; replaces the "5 tries, 15 minutes" values of DL-080 item 10 and Q-154 (a) for the username count): after 3 wrong tries in a row the person waits 5 minutes; after 2 more wrong tries (5 in a row) the person waits 15 minutes; after that, every 2 more wrong tries mean another 15-minute wait, until a correct sign-in. The rest stays as Q-154 (a) says: counted per username, unknown names included; tries during a wait are refused without checking the password and add no time; a correct sign-in clears the count; wrong sign-in codes count; 20 wrong tries per source address in 15 minutes start a 15-minute wait for that address; counts kept in the database; the same wait message whether or not the account exists. Owner's example: Sokha types the wrong password 3 times at 09:00 and waits until 09:05; 2 more wrong tries then mean waiting 15 minutes. Reading recorded (the owner's words "in a row" and "until a correct sign-in"): the username count has no 15-minute window any more; it counts the wrong tries since the last correct sign-in.
- Pre-code design (2026-10-23, fresh session; read-only survey of `local_authentication.py` (`LocalAuthenticationService`, the in-memory `BoundedAuthenticationAttemptLimiter`), `auth_flow.py` (`login`, the session transaction), `auth_api.py` (`AuthenticationRateLimited`, the login route), `app.py` (the 429 handler, `error_response`), the L1d migration `20270121_178` (append-only pattern, definer functions, grants), `test_auth_flow_migration.py` (owner-written rows with times taken back from the database clock), `test_local_authentication.py`, `test_authentication_api.py` (the 429 test) and the test lists of catalog objects):

All three append-only (UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE refused by one trigger function); no runtime table privilege.
  - Three definer functions, READ COMMITTED only, EXECUTE for `prm_runtime` only: `app.sign_in_wait_seconds(username_digest, source_digest)` returns the seconds left (rounded up, at least 1) of the longest active username or source wait, or NULL; `app.record_sign_in_wrong_try(username_digest, source_digest, try_kind)` takes the username lock and then the source lock (transaction advisory locks, always in that order), returns the seconds left of an active wait without recording anything (a try during a wait adds nothing), else records the try and starts a username wait when the wrong tries since the last clear reach 3 (5 minutes), 5, 7, 9 and so on (15 minutes), and a source wait when that source's wrong tries in the last 15 minutes reach 20 (15 minutes), returning the seconds of a wait it started or NULL; `app.clear_sign_in_wrong_tries(username_digest, source_digest, actor_id)` takes the same locks, returns the seconds of an active wait without clearing (fail closed: a wait started by a parallel try wins), else records a clear only when there are wrong tries since the last clear, and returns NULL. Times are the database clock (`clock_timestamp()` after the locks).
  - Keys: the Python side passes sha256 digests, never the typed text: `sha256("username:" + normalize_local_username(username))` and `sha256("source:" + request source)`, so a password typed into the username box is never stored as text (decided under the owner's 2026-10-22 rule).
  - `local_authentication.py`: new protocol `SignInWaitBoundary` (`wait_seconds`, `record_wrong_try`); `LocalAuthenticationService` takes an optional boundary; after the in-memory flood guard it asks for an active wait and, if there is one, refuses without looking the account up or checking the password (audit reason `sign_in_wait`); every refused password check (wrong password, unknown, disabled or unclassified account) records a wrong try; the result carries `wait_seconds`. Without a boundary nothing changes (the committed unit tests keep their fakes).
  - `auth_flow.py`: `_PostgresSignInWaits` (own short READ COMMITTED connection per call, the 5-second timeouts); `login` raises `AuthenticationRateLimited(retry_after_seconds)` when the result carries a wait, else `AuthenticationRejected`; the session transaction calls the clear function first and refuses with a wait when it returns one. A correct password of an account that needs MFA neither counts nor clears (cleared only when the MFA challenge completes in L3c, so a known password cannot be used to reset the count of wrong sign-in codes); binding for L3c: wrong sign-in codes and recovery codes are recorded with their `try_kind`, and the completed challenge clears.
  - `auth_api.py` and `app.py`: `AuthenticationRateLimited` gets an optional `retry_after_seconds`; the existing 429 answer (code `RATE_LIMITED`, the fixed message "Too many requests.") adds `Retry-After` and `Cache-Control: no-store` when it is known. The body is the same for every username, known or not; the sign-in screen writes the wait message (L6). The committed 429 test keeps passing unchanged.

Unit: `test_local_authentication.py` gains tests of the boundary use (no lookup during a wait, wrong tries recorded, a correct password records nothing); `test_auth_flow.py` the digests; `test_authentication_api.py` the `Retry-After` header.

  - Binding for L7 (sharpened by review round 1, security): behind the Vite HTTPS proxy every request comes from 127.0.0.1, so the source count would count everyone together (20 wrong tries from anyone would make everyone wait). uvicorn trusts `X-Forwarded-For` from 127.0.0.1 by default and Vite passes a client-sent one through, so a client could pick its own source or make another address wait. L7 must make the proxy overwrite the client address (`xfwd: true`) and run uvicorn with `--forwarded-allow-ips=127.0.0.1` explicitly, with a test that a client-sent `X-Forwarded-For` is not the recorded source. L7 lands before any shared use.
